description:
## Why

Today `Interactive.state.transcript` is a flat list of heterogeneous structs (UserMessage, AssistantMessage, ToolExecution, BashExecution, CompactionSummaryMessage, plus legacy `{:user, "..."}` tuples). The streaming-cache machinery from `opi-4dx.8`/`.9` lives **inside** the AssistantMessage as a nested `%Transcript{}`. That asymmetry has two consequences:

1. **Per-render ctx allocation.** Every AssistantMessage render builds a fresh `%{theme:, width:, ...}` map, then Transcript.render does a structural-equality check against the stored ctx. trace4 attributes the ~50% `transcript.render` per-call regression vs. trace3 (1.91 → 2.78 ms p50 at msg_count=2 streaming) to that boundary.
2. **No cache for non-AssistantMessage entries.** Finalized UserMessages, completed ToolExecutions, etc. re-render every frame even though their content is fixed.

Both fall out if there's one `%Transcript{}` at the Interactive level, with all entries — including content blocks — as siblings keyed by string ids. ctx is allocated once per frame; finalized blocks of any kind hit the cache uniformly.

## Scope

All work is inside `apps/octo_pi_tui`. Agent-layer events (`MessageStart`/`MessageBlockStart`/`Delta`/`End`/`MessageEnd`) keep their integer `block_id`. Interactive composes the string key `"#{msg_id}:#{block_id}"` at routing time.

## Shape

- `Interactive.state.transcript :: Transcript.t()` replacing the flat list.
- A small id-coiner module (or just inline helpers) that produces stable string keys per entry kind:
  - `"user:#{ts}"`
  - `"assistant_header:#{msg_id}"`
  - `"#{msg_id}:#{block_id}"` for content blocks
  - `"assistant_status:#{msg_id}"` for the trailing error/abort line (only emitted when `stop_reason in [:error, :aborted]`)
  - `"tool:#{tool_call_id}"`, `"bash:#{bash_id}"`, `"compaction:#{ts}"`
- One `Transcript.Renderer` adapter per kind. New: `AssistantHeader` (emits a leading blank + OSC 133 start marker — that's it). `AssistantStatus` (the error/abort line + OSC 133 end). Reuses existing `TextBlock` / `ThinkingBlock` from `.9` for content blocks. Tiny adapters wrapping existing `Component.render/2` for `UserMessage`, `ToolExecution`, `BashExecution`, `CompactionSummaryMessage`.
- Routing in `handle_event`:
  - `MessageStart` → append `AssistantHeader`.
  - `MessageBlockStart` → append a block entry with the right adapter (TextBlock / ThinkingBlock).
  - `MessageBlockDelta` → `Transcript.update` on the block's key. Latest-snapshot-wins coalescing stays the same; `streaming_blocks` map can be removed since the Transcript itself is now the stash (each `update` is O(1) and only mutates one slot).
  - `MessageBlockEnd` → `Transcript.finalize` on the block's key.
  - `MessageEnd` → if `stop_reason in [:error, :aborted]`, append an `AssistantStatus` entry; mark all owned-by-this-msg block entries finalized; mark the AssistantHeader finalized.
- ctx is built once per frame in `Interactive.send_render` (or wherever the render call site lives) and passed to `Transcript.render(t, ctx)`.

## OSC 133 placement

Today `wrap_osc133` injects the start marker on the first line of the AssistantMessage and the end+final markers on the last line. With siblings:
- `AssistantHeader.to_iolist` emits `[OSC133_START, ""]`.
- `AssistantStatus.to_iolist` (when present) emits `[error_line, OSC133_END, OSC133_FINAL]`.
- When no status entry exists (the common `:stop` path), the OSC end+final markers attach to the last block of the message — either via a small post-finalize "stamp the last block's renderer" step or a wrapper renderer that knows it's the last block. Pick whichever is cleanest at implementation time; both work.

## Acceptance

- `Interactive.state.transcript` is a `%Transcript{}`.
- All transcript mutations go through `Transcript.append` / `update` / `finalize`. No `List.replace_at`, `Enum.find_index`, or `apply_streaming_blocks` content-list rebuild on the hot path.
- `find_last_assistant` becomes a one-liner over `Transcript.order` looking for an `AssistantHeader` whose matching `AssistantStatus` (or last block) hasn't crossed a turn boundary.
- `transcript.render` per-call duration at streaming msg_count=2 is back to or below trace3's 1.91 ms p50.
- `streaming_blocks` map can be deleted — the Transcript itself absorbs the per-block stash.
- All existing TUI integration tests pass post-migration; a new test exercises a multi-turn run with finalized history to assert per-render `transcript.render` cost is flat in finalized message count.

## Tests

- Existing `interactive_test.exs`, `interactive_compaction_test.exs`, `interactive_stream_coalescing_test.exs` migrate cleanly.
- New: streaming a long markdown response while holding ≥ 5 finalized prior messages; assert `markdown.render` telemetry fires only on the streaming message's pending tail.
- New: out-of-order `MessageBlockDelta` events (different `block_id`s within the same message) render in the right order via the string key.
- New: an aborted turn produces a transcript with header + blocks + status entries in that order.

## Notes

Discovered during the `.10` post-merge review: the nested-Transcript design was a hedge against having to write Renderer adapters for every entry kind. With `<msg_id>:<block_id>` strings as keys the adapter cost is small and mechanical, and the abstraction earns its keep at both levels rather than just inside AssistantMessage.
title: Flatten Interactive's transcript onto a single top-level Transcript
